eyebrow: Enterprise Security Architecture, GRC & Risk Management · Chapter One
titlePlain: Security Architecture as a Set of
subtitle: Lesson 2 · Tradeoffs, Not a Checklist

code:
Checklist thinking:
  "Is MFA enabled? Yes / No."
  More controls present = always better.

Reality:
  Every control has a cost.
  The right amount of security differs
  by business, and by system.
caption: A checklist can't represent cost — architecture has to.

eyebrow: Every control carries three real costs

steps.label: Friction
steps.sub: a usability/time tax on legitimate users and workflows, every day

steps.label: Money
steps.sub: licensing, infrastructure, and headcount — ongoing, not one-time

steps.label: Complexity
steps.sub: a new moving part that can itself fail, drift, or become a target

code:
No controls -> foundational baseline:
  huge risk reduction, cheap.

Baseline -> the last few % of theoretical risk:
  exponentially more expensive and disruptive,
  for a shrinking return.
caption: A checklist can't see this curve. An architect has to pick a point on it.

steps.label: Unbearable friction
steps.sub: pushes legitimate users toward shadow IT

steps.label: Shadow IT
steps.sub: personal cloud storage, unofficial chat, shared-password spreadsheets

steps.label: Risk acceptance
steps.sub: the honest alternative: document the gap, name who owns the residual risk

subtitle: Layering this same tradeoff thinking across an entire organization.
